title: Learning Atmospheric Boundary Layer Turbulence
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
parameterization_target: vertical turbulent fluxes of heat, TKE, and passive tracers
testbed_rationale: High-resolution LES dataset across six shear-to-convection regimes coarse-grained to 1.5 km, designed specifically for training and validating subgrid vertical turbulent flux parameterizations with processing scripts and neural network models archived on Zenodo.
pain_points: Scale and grid dependence: trained on a single horizontal coarse-graining scale (1.5 km, gray zone) and fixed vertical grid discretization rather than being scale-adaptive or grid-agnostic
Extrapolation failure when generalizing to lower instability parameters (near-neutral / strongly shear-driven regimes) due to lack of self-similarity
Latent space entanglement in standard VAEs, necessitating a specialized dual-branch encoder-decoder architecture to separate horizontal and vertical TKE modes
Inability to account for horizontal transport and heterogeneity with a 1D vertical column approach, leading to smoothing of individual profile fluctuations
extraction_notes: The document is an ESSOAr preprint submitted to JAMES. The Open Research section notes that ML tools and scripts for pre- and post-processing are released at Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.8039033).
